parts.markdown:
Use our free **Rhode Island paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Rhode Island income tax, Social Security, Medicare and Temporary Disability Insurance contributions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, choose your payment frequency and customize your withholding information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Rhode Island's payroll system includes employee-funded disability insurance, making its paycheck calculations different from those in many other states.

Whether you work in Providence, Warwick, Cranston, Pawtucket or another Rhode Island community, understanding your net income can help you compare job offers, manage expenses and establish realistic financial goals.

## How to Use the Rhode Island Paycheck Calculator

Start by selecting annual salary or hourly wages.

Enter your earnings before taxes and deductions, then choose your payment frequency.

Enter the federal and Rhode Island income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Enter any Temporary Disability Insurance withheld under Benefits in Advanced settings, under Other deductions.

Add retirement contributions, healthcare premiums and other employee deductions. Enter the full tax amounts, including any extra withholding.

Review your estimated paycheck breakdown to understand your gross earnings, individual taxes and remaining take-home pay.

Use your latest payroll statement and withholding certificates for greater accuracy.

## Rhode Island Payroll Taxes in 2026

Your actual paycheck depends on your taxable income, withholding exemptions, employee benefits and employment circumstances.

The [Rhode Island Division of Taxation](https://tax.ri.gov/) provides official information about state income tax and employer withholding.

## How Rhode Island State Income Tax Works

Rhode Island applies progressive individual income tax rates of 3.75%, 4.75% and 5.99%.

Different portions of applicable taxable wages may therefore be subject to different withholding rates.

The state's official employer percentage tables apply to all withholding filing status categories, with applicable adjustments for employee withholding exemptions.

These are employer withholding brackets, not annual individual income tax return brackets.

Read the official [2026 Rhode Island withholding booklet](https://tax.ri.gov/sites/g/files/xkgbur541/files/2025-12/2026%20Withholding%20Tax%20Booklet.pdf) for all payroll frequencies and calculation instructions.

## Understanding Rhode Island Withholding Exemptions

Rhode Island employees generally provide state withholding information through Form RI W-4.

Each ordinary withholding exemption has an annual value of $1,000, subject to an income limit.

The exemption value becomes zero when wages exceed the applicable high-income threshold.

For biweekly payroll, that threshold is $11,184.62 in 2026. The corresponding published annual threshold is $290,800.

These limits mean high-income employees may receive different withholding treatment despite claiming the same number of exemptions as lower-income employees.

Consult pages 9–10 of the official withholding booklet for the appropriate payroll-period thresholds.

## How to Calculate Rhode Island Income Tax Withholding

Consider an employee receiving $2,500 in biweekly taxable wages and claiming one qualifying state withholding exemption.

Applicable exemption: $38.46.

Adjusted taxable wages:

$2,500 − $38.46 = $2,461.54.

Because this amount falls within the first biweekly percentage bracket, apply the 3.75% rate.

$2,461.54 × 3.75% = approximately $92.31.

This example assumes ordinary taxable employment, no additional withholding and no high-income exemption restriction.

Employees with different withholding elections may have different deductions.

## Rhode Island Temporary Disability Insurance

Rhode Island's Temporary Disability Insurance program provides financial assistance to eligible workers experiencing qualifying non-work-related illness or injury.

The employee payroll contribution also supports the state's Temporary Caregiver Insurance program.

For 2026, the employee contribution rate is 1.1% of covered earnings, up to an annual wage ceiling of $100,000.

The maximum standard annual employee contribution is:

$100,000 × 0.011 = $1,100.

These amounts assume the annual taxable wage ceiling has not been reached.

Visit the official [Rhode Island TDI and TCI tax information page](https://dlt.ri.gov/individuals/temporary-disability-caregiver-insurance/claimants/tdi-and-tci-tax-information) for additional details.

## Rhode Island TDI Wage Limit Example

Suppose an employee has already earned $99,000 in covered wages during 2026 and receives another paycheck containing $2,500.

Only $1,000 remains below the $100,000 annual wage ceiling.

The TDI deduction for that paycheck would therefore be:

$1,000 × 1.1% = $11.

Applying the rate to the entire paycheck would produce an incorrect deduction of $27.50.

Once the annual wage ceiling is reached with an employer, ordinary contributions generally stop for the remainder of the calendar year.

Employees who change employers may qualify for a refund of excess contributions under applicable rules.

The [Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training employer tax information](https://dlt.ri.gov/employers/employer-tax-unit) provides annual contribution rates and wage bases.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Rhode Island Paychecks

Federal income tax withholding depends on your taxable earnings, filing status, payment frequency and Form W-4 information.

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered wages to Social Security, subject to the 2026 annual wage ceiling of $184,500.

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered wages.

Employers generally withhold an additional 0.9% when Medicare-covered wages paid by that employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

Review [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t), [IRS Publication 15](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) and the [Social Security Administration wage ceiling information](https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html) for official federal payroll rules.

## Rhode Island Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Suppose you earn $26 per hour and work 40 regular hours plus six qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings: $1,040.

Overtime earnings: $234.

Total gross earnings: $1,274.

If all earnings are covered by ordinary disability insurance and the annual ceiling has not been reached, the TDI deduction would be approximately $14.01.

Applicable federal and state taxes would also reduce the paycheck.

Consult the [Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training](https://dlt.ri.gov/) and [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for applicable employment requirements.

## Does Rhode Island Have Local Income Taxes?

Rhode Island municipalities generally do not impose separate personal wage income taxes on ordinary employee earnings.

However, employees working across state borders may encounter additional withholding obligations.

For example, a Rhode Island resident working in Massachusetts may have Massachusetts withholding and Rhode Island annual tax filing responsibilities.

Applicable tax credits may reduce double taxation.

A standard Rhode Island paycheck estimate may not fully capture complicated interstate employment arrangements.

## Managing Your Rhode Island Take-Home Income

Use estimated net income to establish realistic spending limits for housing, transportation, groceries, utilities, insurance and debt payments.

Employees approaching the TDI wage ceiling may notice an increase in their take-home pay when their employer stops collecting the ordinary contribution.

Avoid treating this temporary increase as a permanent salary adjustment because annual contribution limits reset in the next calendar year.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help establish a savings target, while our [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) can help compare employment offers.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Rhode Island's income tax rate in 2026?

Rhode Island uses progressive withholding rates of 3.75%, 4.75% and 5.99%. Actual deductions depend on applicable wage thresholds and withholding exemptions.

### How much is Rhode Island TDI in 2026?

The employee contribution rate is 1.1% of covered wages up to $100,000, producing a maximum standard annual contribution of $1,100.

### Why did my Rhode Island disability insurance deduction change?

The rate, annual wage ceiling and your year-to-date covered earnings affect the deduction. Rhode Island changed both its contribution rate and wage ceiling for 2026.
